To your queries-
The initial reboot was triggered from the OCPP Backend:
2.

FO]:tcp reader: poweroff requested again, ignored..." messages.?
I checked the SCB Logs of 170003620 there are no SCB entries at this time stamp.

4.

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: ID0406379-DC/Si-D/AT-[MP / S5 170003620] Connector availability update with faulted CRM:00921001540
additional_info.body:
Hello Johannes,
Hope you are doing well.
We apologize for the delayed reply. As we checked the logs on both SCC and SCB, we correlated them with the given timestamp and observed that...
As we checked the logs for the timestamp 15:38:56 (UTC), it showed as faulted on
SCB
, and the same fault was recorded in the SCC logs. The fault event was triggered due to an authorization issue. Maybe the ID tag is not whitelisted.
2025-02-18T15:38:56.768346+00:00 sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/f5a51e691eb6[733]: OCPP: Send command: StatusNotification (763fa22b-5cc7-44af-9df2-aa365cbaf4b2) - {"connectorId":2,"errorCode":"InternalError","status":"Faulted"}
2.In this case, when the connector availability became faulted on SCC at 02:30:09 PM (local time), we checked the logs on SCB, where it showed as suspended and we could not find any fault message during that time. We are further investigating with the concerned team and will get back to you soon with an update.
If you have any further queries, please do notify us.
Regards,
Beerpal Singh
eMobility Support
